newsitem.title: GERMANY: Sony's German unit to return to profit in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Sony's German unit to return to profit in 96/97.

text.p: The German unit of Japanese electronics giant Sony Corp will report a return to profitability in its 1996/97 business year, Josef Brauner, chairman of Sony Deutschland GmbH said on Friday.

Turnover at Sony Deutschland increased nine percent to around 1.6 billion marks between April and December 1996, Braunau said in an advance copy of an interview with the Koelner Stadt-Anzeiger newspaper to be published tomorrow.
"In 1996/97 we will see a clear return to the black," said Braunau.

Sony Deutschland would report single-digit million mark profits in the year to the end of March 1996/97, after notching up total losses in the previous three years of around 35 million marks, Braunau said.

"I would like to put these losses into context. Compared with the rest of the sector we got off very lightly. We have cut a lot of the fat that we put on in previous years and have reduced costs by 100 million marks in the last three years," said Braunau.
Braunau ruled out the possibility of a takeover of the troubled electronics group INTERRUPTED
Among Sony's main success stories in 1996 was its "Play Station" computer game product, which had risen to market leadership within two years, Braunau said.
The market for traditional home entertainment products in Germany was shrinking and the future lay in combining the audio, video, telecommunications and computer sectors, he said.

Braunau went on to say the new Sony personal computer, recently launched in the U.S., would probably hit the Japanese market in 1997 and arrive on German and other European markets in 1998. -- Frankfurt Newsroom +49 69 756525
